objective: Performing schedule risk analysis (what-if scenarios, Monte Carlo simulation) to test whether milestones are achievable within risk tolerance
secondaryObjectives: Identifying critical and near-critical paths (Critical Path Method, Critical Chain, PERT, Monte Carlo simulation)
Estimating activity durations using three-point, parametric, analogous, or PERT techniques

sources.cite: PMI, PMI Scheduling Professional (PMI-SP) Examination Content Outline (2012, revision mark 4/20): Schedule Strategy 14%, Planning and Development 31%, Monitoring and Controlling 35%, Closeout 6%, Stakeholder Communications 14%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a copy of PMI's PDF hosted by a consultancy. Relevant text: Monitoring and Controlling Task 3 'Perform schedule analysis and audit ... in order to identify and report project schedule, status, changes, impacts or issues'; Task 5 'Incorporate approved risk mitigation activities into the schedule, by utilizing defined change control processes'; Task 6 'Update the schedule model and document schedule baseline changes, received through formal change-control processes'. The objective wording here is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's clinic-fitout-variance-pmisp (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the scheduler for the new surgical wing at Brookvale General, a fictional hospital. The deterministic schedule finishes 12 September against a 30 September contract milestone. The sponsor's risk tolerance: at least 80% confidence of meeting it.
handover: Three parallel paths (mechanical, electrical, medical gas) merge at commissioning.
Durations so far are single-point estimates.
howItWorks: The dashboard shows the commitments, the work items, the risks and issues, the people's support and the milestones.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each status meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: the sponsor commits the hospital's opening to 1 October on the 'safe' date.
Week 3: the medical gas valves arrive late; commissioning slips past 30 September and liquidated damages start.
Week 4: crews fill the padded durations; real progress is invisible and the schedule loses credibility with the hospital.

effects.log: Week 1: the sponsor asks if 30 September is safe.

choices.label: Run a Monte Carlo simulation on three-point estimates across the network: P50 is 24 September, P80 is 4 October

effects.log: The simulation shows P80 after the milestone.

choices.feedback: Merging parallel paths adds risk a single-point CPM date hides (merge bias); the simulation shows the confidence.

choices.label: Use PERT on the critical path only
choices.feedback: Better than single points, but ignores the other paths merging.

choices.label: Report 12 September as safe: 18 days of margin
choices.feedback: A single-point date ignores uncertainty and merge bias.

nearPrompt.title: Which path drives the risk?
nearPrompt.context: Medical gas is critical in 55% of iterations, though not on the deterministic critical path.

choices.label: Treat medical gas as a near-critical driver: pre-order the long-lead valves and add a second certified crew in August
choices.feedback: The criticality index shows which path really drives the finish.

choices.label: Accelerate the deterministic critical path (electrical)
choices.feedback: That path is critical in only 30% of iterations; the main driver is untouched.

choices.label: Ignore it: medical gas isn't on the critical path
choices.feedback: The path most likely to delay the finish is left alone.

choices.label: Add 30 days of hidden padding to every activity and report 'on track'

effects.log: Padding is hidden in the activities.

choices.feedback: Hidden padding destroys the schedule's credibility and gets consumed (Parkinson's law).

reflection.question: Write the schedule risk report: how likely 30 September is, what drives the risk and what you did about it.

scoring.modelReasoning: A deterministic critical-path date ignores uncertainty and merge bias, where parallel paths joining make a late finish more likely. Schedule risk analysis runs Monte Carlo on three-point estimates to give confidence levels (P50, P80) to compare with the risk tolerance; the criticality index exposes near-critical paths that often drive the finish. Responses are targeted at the drivers and the analysis is rerun and reported openly.
